title: Svayamprabha's welcome
hookLine: lost and thirsty in the dark, then a golden city and a welcome
carry: atithi devo bhava: the guest is god
last: NAMA: THE NAME CARRIES THE ONE IT NAMES.

cards: The southern party is having a terrible time. They've searched the Vindhya hills, forest after forest, cave after cave. Nothing.

Now they're lost, hungry and desperately thirsty, in dry country with no stream in sight, and the month is running out. Then they see birds flying out of a hole in the hillside: cranes, geese, waterbirds, their wings wet.
Where there are wet birds, there's water somewhere. So in they go.

teach.b: The cave is dark and overgrown with creepers. Valmiki calls it Rikshabila, the bear's hole. Hanuman goes first.
The monkeys hold on to one another in the pitch black and go deeper, with no idea what's at the end. And then light.
A place that shouldn't exist underground: golden trees glowing like fire, palaces of gold and silver, lotus pools, heaps of fruit and honey.
In the middle sits a woman ascetic, dressed in bark and black antelope skin, shining with her own light. Hanuman approaches with joined palms: whose place is this?

teach.h: A GOLDEN CITY BUILT BY MAYA.
teach.b: It was built by Maya, she says, the great architect of the demons. He lived here with Hema, a celestial dancer, until Indra killed him. I am Svayamprabha, daughter of Merusavarni, and I keep it for my friend.
Then comes what she does next. She doesn't question them or test them. Eat first, she says.
Drink. Rest. Then tell me your story.
That order is an old Hindu teaching.

teach.h: ATITHI DEVO BHAVA: THE GUEST IS GOD.
teach.b: The Taittiriya Upanishad sends students home from their teacher with a few lines to live by, and one of them is atithi devo bhava: let the guest be a god to you.
A guest arrives, and you treat them the way you'd treat the divine at your door: water, a seat, food, before any questions. Svayamprabha doesn't know these monkeys. They could be anyone.
She feeds them anyway. That's why, in so many Hindu homes, you can't get through the door without someone handing you water and a plate before you've even sat down.

how: In many Hindu homes a guest is offered water on arrival and fed before any business, and families often quote atithi devo bhava for it. Svayamprabha is remembered as one of the Ramayana's ascetic women, alongside Shabari.

o: 'self-shining': the ascetic of the hidden golden city
the demon architect who built a city underground
a celestial dancer who owns the golden cave

games.q: the hidden city — tap the pairs.
p: the bear's hole, the cave's name
the demon architect who built the city
the celestial dancer it belongs to

s: the monkeys find the cave by following wet birds
waterbirds flying out with wet wings meant water inside.
Svayamprabha questions them before she feeds them
she tells them to eat and drink first, then asks their story.
'atithi devo bhava' means: let the guest be a god to you
it's from the Taittiriya Upanishad, and it's why Hindu hosts feed a guest first.

games.q: you're Svayamprabha. starving strangers stumble into your hidden city. they could be anyone. what does a Hindu host do first?
o: question them until you're sure they're safe.
water, food and rest first, then their story.
show them the way out before they eat anything.
games.why: she feeds them first: atithi devo bhava, the guest is a god at your door.

practice: If there's water near you, take one slow sip; if not, just notice your mouth and throat.
Breathe in and remember the parched monkeys following wet wings into the dark; breathe out and feel what it is to be fed before anyone asks who you are.
Then think of one person who'll come through your door, or to your desk, this week, and decide what you'll offer them first: water, tea, a seat. That's atithi devo bhava, the way Hindu homes live it.

wordCard.voice: Svayamprabha, 'self-shining': the ascetic who keeps a golden city hidden in a cave, and feeds the lost monkeys before asking who they are.

orig.note: Sanskrit svayamprabhā: 'self-shining', from svayam (by oneself) + prabhā (light, radiance).

carryVoice: Your line: atithi devo bhava, the guest is god. Svayamprabha fed them before she asked their names. Until tomorrow.
